name: remote_service_slow
title: The far end is slow
description: DNS, the router and the path are all healthy. Only the service being contacted is slow, so the answer is that nothing is wrong with your network.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 82 ms to send their first byte, about 63 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.

card.title: Your router is slow to respond
card.summary: Round trips to your own router are taking 4 ms with 1 ms of variation. On a healthy home network this is a couple of milliseconds and steady, so something local is loading it up.
remediation: Check whether something on your network is saturating the connection, such as a large upload or a backup.
Power cycle your router: unplug it for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
Plug in an ethernet cable for anything important in the next few minutes.

evidence.label: mean absolute deviation of gateway RTT within the probe burst

card.summary: The signals that changed are on this machine rather than on the network around it: CPU 28%, 0.5% of connections retransmitted.

Restart this device's network adapter.
Check for an update to this device's network adapter driver.

card.title: The far end is slow to answer
card.summary: Your router and the path out to the internet both look normal, but the services we test are taking 83 ms to send their first byte, about 65 ms more than the network itself explains.
remediation: Check whether other sites are fine; if they are, the problem is at the far end and not with your connection.
Check the service's own status page.
Wait a few minutes; this often clears on its own.
